title: Amount Input
summary: A money field that groups digits as you type, spells the amount out and flags an amount about ten times off the usual one.
description: Groups digits live with Intl.NumberFormat (lakh/crore for en-IN), spells the amount cheque-style, and when you pass `typical` warns about an amount 10× or more above or below it, with a one-tap fix. Reports the value as a JavaScript number.
catches: An extra or missing zero, when the amount is 10× or more off the `typical` value you pass
Hard-to-read long numbers, by grouping digits as you type (Indian grouping for en-IN)
Misread amounts, by spelling the amount out in words
Leading zeros and decimals beyond the currency's precision
limits: The warning needs a `typical` amount and only fires at a fixed 10× ratio; a 5× or 9× slip is not flagged, and the ratio shown is rounded down (15.9× shows as 15×)
onValueChange returns a JavaScript float, and up to 15 integer digits are kept, which is beyond safe float precision with decimals; extra digits are dropped silently
A paste in another locale's format is misread without warning (in en-IN, "1.250,50" becomes 1.25)
Words are hard-coded English ("Rupees … only", "paise"), and non-INR unit names use the plural form, so 1 USD reads "One US Dollars"
Defaults to en-IN and INR; set locale and currency for other markets
a11y: Warnings are in an aria-live="polite" region and the fix button returns focus to the input
The animated read-back respects prefers-reduced-motion (motion's useReducedMotion)
Note: aria-describedby always references the words element, even when words are hidden
server: Validate amount and currency on the server, derive payable amounts from trusted data and use idempotency keys; this warning is a review prompt, not a correctness check.
